item.title: Joshua Wong, face of Hong Kong's pro-democracy protests, jailed for 10 years
item.description:
Wong, 30, has been imprisoned since 2020 and is the only activist in Hong Kong prosecuted twice under national security law Exclusive: Joshua Wong laments city’s fate from inside maximum security prison Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong has been sentenced to 10 years in prison after earlier pleading guilty to “foreign collusion”, his second conviction under a national security law that critics say has been used to silence political opposition in the city. Wong, who rose to prominence as the teenage face of Hong Kong’s 2014 pro-democracy demonstrations, submitted his guilty plea in September. He had been accused of working with the exiled Hong Kong activist Nathan Law to urge foreign powers to impose sanctions, blockades or other hostile measures against China. Continue reading...

item.title: Midterms 2026: Data Centers Out, Reproductive Freedom In
item.description:
People across America rejected data centers during last night’s midterm election. Proposals related to data centers were explicitly on the ballot in more than 40 races across 13 states. People voted against data centers in 38 of them and counting. Six cities voted to ban data centers outright and 12 put limits on the amount of megawatts such buildings could draw. In addition to specific ballot measures, candidates who supported data centers lost across the country. One of the most striking repudiations of pro data center politicians was in Texas, where Gregg Abbott lost a bid for a fourth term as governor. Abbott had made Texas a data center friendly place. item.title: Voters Reject Industry-Backed Ballot Measures With Big Environmental Stakes
item.description:
Even as abortion was not a top issue for voters in the midterm elections, Americans repeatedly rejected ballot initiatives and candidates they perceived as anti-abortion — a sign that reproductive rights have become a stand-in for broader questions of trust in lawmakers. In Missouri, voters rejected a ballot measure advanced by the state’s Republican leadership that would have overturned the abortion rights protections voters enshrined just two years ago . In Maine, voters turned against 30-year incumbent Republican Sen. Susan Collins after Democrat Troy Jackson hammered her over her vote to confirm Brett Kavanaugh, the Supreme Court justice who helped overturn Roe v. Wade in 2022. Jackson argued that the vote demonstrated poor judgment and that Collins could not be trusted to represent her constituents’ interests. item.title: Mike Johnson will step aside as top House Republican next Congress
item.description:
Republican women in Iowa, who once enjoyed gender parity in congressional representation, will have no seats when the next Congress is sworn in, losses that reflect a bigger trend on an election night where Democrats across the country flipped enough seats to take control of the House and Senate. Before Election Day, GOP women held a Senate seat and two of Iowa’s four congressional seats. After Tuesday, they will have no representation in either chamber, according to projections from Decision Desk HQ. GOP Sen. Joni Ernst had decided to not seek reelection, and Iowa’s Ashley Hinson lost the race for her seat to Democrat Josh Turek. It wasn’t just in Iowa where Republican women lost: The longest-serving Republican woman senator, Maine’s Susan Collins, fell to Democrat Troy Jackson. item.title: Vote counting underway in critical South Africa elections
item.description:
Party expected to get less than a third of the vote amid frustration over water outages and power cuts The African National Congress is on course for a bruising result in South Africa’s local elections on Wednesday as voters go to the polls amid deep discontent over water outages, power cuts and crumbling infrastructure. The former liberation movement, which Nelson Mandela led to power in 1994 at the end of apartheid as South Africa’s first black president, is still likely to be the largest party. However, polls showed it getting less than a third of the vote, down from 45.6% at the last municipal elections in 2021 and 40.2% in 2024’s national elections . Continue reading...

item.title: Trump’s No Good Very Bad Day
item.description:
A blue wave engulfed Republicans in this year’s midterm elections. Democrats throughout the country soundly defeated GOP candidates, giving them at least 54 seats in the US Senate and a majority in the House of Representatives. But it was where they won that was so shocking. item.title: Fact check: Examining viral narratives after the US midterm elections
item.description:
It was a drubbing on a scale that neither side saw coming: Democrats pummeled Republicans across the battleground map and into some of the most MAGA-friendly terrain in the country. Why it matters: The results were an emphatic rejection of Donald Trump's second term in office — and set the stage for two years of corruption investigations and legislative frustration for the lame-duck president. Here's a rundown of what you need to know about last night's historic GOP beatdown. The size of the Dem majorities It was clear early in the night that Democrats would flip the Senate. Few predicted how big their majority would end up. Democrats will have at least 54 Senate seats, and another two — in Alaska and Mississippi — were too close to call early Wednesday. item.description:
Well, that sucked. A blue tsunami. The Republicans who wanted to win were like Richard Chamberlain in the movie “The Last Wave,” waiting on the shore for our doom, or for the Gen Xers in the crowd, Tea Leoni and Maximilian Schell on the beach in “Deep Impact,” just watching that gigantic wave come at them. It was brutal and pretty unprecedented. The big question this morning is very simple: What the hell happened? I want to start with what didn’t happen, what this wasn’t about. item.title: Democrats Seize Congress, Statehouses in Referendum on the Economy
item.description:
More than 30 years ago, then-Illinois state Rep. Carol Moseley Braun became the first Black woman elected to the U.S. Senate in a watershed year for women candidates. This year, another woman from Illinois — Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton — made history again. Her win makes her the fifth Black woman ever elected to the U.S. Senate and cements Illinois as the first state to have two women of color in the Senate at the same time. Her win also guarantees that, for the first time in history, three Black women will serve simultaneously in the upper chamber. Decision Desk HQ projected that Angie Nixon , the Democratic nominee for Senate in Florida, will lose to incumbent Ashley Moody. item.title: South Korea says it will expand naval operations closer to strait of Hormuz
item.description:
Seoul to seek parliamentary approval to extend anti-piracy Cheonghae unit’s area to about 650km from the vital strait after criticism from Donald Trump on Iran war support South Korea plans to expand the operations ⁠of its anti-piracy unit to waters closer to the strait of Hormuz, its defence ministry has said, after pressure from Donald Trump to ⁠provide support for his war in Iran. The government is to submit a motion to parliament that would expand the Cheonghae unit’s area of operation to waters near the port of Duqm in Oman, which is about 650km (403 miles) away from the strait. The motion also needs to be approved by ‌President Lee Jae Myung and the cabinet. Continue reading...
